candidate.title: smMIP
candidate.scope: Illumina’s single connected smMIP schematic, titled smMIP on the assigned card and introduced in the image as Single Molecule Molecular Inversion Probes (smMIPs) for detecting low frequency targets. The candidate collection page matches by its heading “smMIP: Single-Molecule Molecular Inversion Probes” and caption “A schematic overview of smMIPs.” The architecture runs from tagged probe capture of a genomic region through copying/closure, exonuclease selection, indexed PCR, sequencing, molecular-tag read grouping and consensus. Hiatt et al. (2013), Figure 1 and relevant full-text Methods clarify the probe-circle topology and indexing interfaces; details specific to that implementation are identified as such. The Gene icon identifies the biological target, and the fan of same-tag reads illustrates amplified descendants rather than alternative workflows or a physical sample split. smMIP and plural smMIPs name one assay. The collection’s review/application citations and the card’s kit list do not define additional schematic targets.

The primary Figure 1 calls the combined method smMIP and supports the depicted probe capture, gap-fill/ligation, exonuclease/PCR and tag-consensus architecture. Generic MIP capture is an embedded component, not another diagram target. Hiatt’s exact probe/tag design and readout clarification are used at this implementation interface without claiming that all later smMIP adaptations share every preparation detail.
